items.readable_text:
Content:
How do we evaluate an integral like [MATH: \displaystyle \int \dfrac{2x-1}{(x+2)(x-3)} \textrm{d}x?]

Content:
First of all, note that the integrand can be converted into a sum of partial fractions:
[MATH: \dfrac{2x-1}{(x+2)(x-3)}=\dfrac{A}{(x+2)} +\dfrac{B}{(x-3)}]

Content:
If we can figure out the partial fractions, then we can integrate each of the partial fractions using the natural logarithm.

Content:
So, let's compute the partial fractions. If we multiply the above equation by [MATH: (x+2)(x-3),] we get

Content:
[MATH: 2x − 1|= A(x − 3) + B(x + 2).]

Content:
The expression above must hold for all values of [MATH: x.] Plugging in [MATH: x=-2,] we can eliminate [MATH: B] and solve for [MATH: A\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: 2(− 2) − 1|= A(− 2 − 3) + B(− 2 + 2); − 5|= A(− 5) + B(0); A|= 1.]

Content:
On the other hand, plugging in [MATH: x=3,] we can eliminate [MATH: A] and solve for [MATH: B\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: 2(3) − 1|= A(3 − 3) + B(3 + 2); 5|= A(0) + B(5); B|= 1.]

Content:
Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{2x-1}{(x+2)(x-3)} = \dfrac{1}{(x+2)} +\dfrac{1}{(x-3)}.]

Content:
Finally, we can integrate each of the partial fractions separately:
[MATH: ∫(2x − 1)/((x + 2)(x − 3))dx|= ∫((1)/(x + 2) + (1)/(x − 3))dx; = ∫(1)/(x + 2)dx + ∫(1)/(x − 3)dx; = \ln|x + 2|+ \ln|x − 3|+ C.]

Content:
And we're done!

First, we note that the denominator of the integrand can be factored as [MATH: x^2+3x-4 = (x-1)(x+4) \,.]

So, the integrand can be converted into a sum of partial fractions,

[MATH: (5x)/(x^{2} + 3x − 4)|= (5x)/((x − 1)(x + 4)); = (A)/((x − 1)) + (B)/((x + 4)),]

which gives

[MATH: 5x|= A(x + 4) + B(x − 1).]

Plugging in [MATH: x=-4,] we can eliminate [MATH: A] and solve for [MATH: B\mathbin{:}] [MATH: 5(− 4)|= A(− 4 + 4) + B(− 4 − 1); − 20|= − 5B; B|= 4.] On the other hand, by plugging in [MATH: x=1,] we can eliminate [MATH: B] and solve for [MATH: A\mathbin{:}] [MATH: 5(1)|= A(1 + 4) + B(1 − 1); 5|= 5A; A|= 1.] Therefore, [MATH: \dfrac{5x}{x^2+3x-4} = \dfrac{1}{(x-1)} +\dfrac{4}{(x+4)}.]

Finally, we integrate, and we get [MATH: ∫(5x)/(x^{2} + 3x − 4)dx|= ∫((1)/(x − 1) + (4)/(x + 4))dx; = ∫(1)/(x − 1)dx + 4∫(1)/(x + 4)dx; = \ln|x − 1|+ 4\ln|x + 4|+ C.]

sections.normalized_html:
We'll work out the indefinite integral first and then proceed with the definite integral.

First, we note that a denominator of the integrand can be factored as [MATH: 4x^2-1 = (2x+1)(2x-1) \,.]

So the integrand can be converted into a sum of partial fractions,

[MATH: (2x + 3)/(4x^{2} − 1)|= (2x + 3)/((2x + 1)(2x − 1)); = (A)/((2x + 1)) + (B)/((2x − 1)),] which gives [MATH: 2x + 3|= A(2x − 1) + B(2x + 1).]

Plugging in [MATH: x=\dfrac{1}{2},] we can eliminate [MATH: A] and solve for [MATH: B\mathbin{:}] [MATH: 2((1)/(2)) + 3|= A(2((1)/(2)) − 1) + B(2((1)/(2)) + 1); 4|= 2B; B|= 2.] On the other hand, plugging in [MATH: x=-\dfrac{1}{2},] we can eliminate [MATH: B] and solve for [MATH: A\mathbin{:}] [MATH: 2(− (1)/(2)) + 3|= A(2(− (1)/(2)) − 1) + B(2(− (1)/(2)) + 1); 2|= − 2A; A|= − 1.]

Therefore, [MATH: \dfrac{2x+3}{4x^2-1} = -\dfrac{1}{(2x+1)} +\dfrac{2}{(2x-1)}.]

Now, we integrate and get [MATH: ∫(2x + 3)/(4x^{2} − 1)dx|= ∫(− (1)/((2x + 1)) + (2)/((2x − 1)))dx; = − ∫(1)/(2x + 1)dx + 2∫(1)/(2x − 1)dx; = − (1)/(2)\ln|2x + 1|+ 2((1)/(2)\ln|2x − 1|) + C; = − (1)/(2)\ln|2x + 1|+ \ln|2x − 1|+ C.]

We can simplify the result using the laws of logarithms, as follows:

[MATH: ∫(2x + 3)/(4x^{2} − 1)dx|= − (1)/(2)\ln|2x + 1|+ \ln|2x − 1|+ C; = \ln|(1)/(sqrt(2x + 1))|+ \ln|2x − 1|+ C; = \ln|(2x − 1)/(sqrt(2x + 1))|+ C]

Finally, the definite integral is

[MATH: ∫_{1}^{4}(2x + 3)/(4x^{2} − 1)dx|= \ln|(2x − 1)/(sqrt(2x + 1))|_{1}^{4}; = \ln ((7)/(3)) − \ln ((1)/(sqrt(3))); = \ln ((7)/(3)) + \ln (sqrt(3)); = \ln ((7sqrt(3))/(3)).]

Item 2 — Example: Calculating an Indefinite Integral of a Rational Function Using Partial Fractions

[MATH: \dfrac{5x}{x^2+3x-4} = \dfrac{1}{(x-1)} +\dfrac{4}{(x+4)}.]
